sp.p: As it were, to ride day and night; and not to deliberate, not to remember, not to have patience to shift me,--

sp.speaker: Shal.
sp.p: It is best, certain.

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: But to stand stained with travel, and sweating with desire to see him; thinking of nothing else, putting all affairs else inoblivion, as if there were nothing else to be done but to see him.

sp.speaker: Pist.
sp.p: 'Tis 'semper idem,' for 'obsque hoc nihil est:' 'tis all in every part.

sp.speaker: Shal.
sp.p: 'Tis so, indeed.

sp.speaker: Pist.
sp.p:
My knight, I will inflame thy noble liver, And make thee rage. Thy Doll, and Helen of thy noble thoughts, Is in base durance and contagious prison; Haled thither By most mechanical and dirty hand: Rouse up revenge from ebon den with fell Alecto's
snake, For Doll is in. Pistol speaks nought but truth.

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p:
I will deliver her.
[Shouts within, and the trumpets sound.

sp.speaker: Pist.
sp.p:
There roar'd the sea, and trumpet clangor
sounds.
Enter the KING and his train, the LORD
CHIEF-JUSTICE among them.

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: God save thy grace, King Hal! my royal Hal!

sp.speaker: Pist.
sp.p: The heavens thee guard and keep, most royal imp of fame!

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: God save thee, my sweet boy!

sp.speaker: King.
sp.p:
My lord chief-justice, speak to that
vain man.

sp.speaker: Ch. Just.
sp.p:
Have you your wits? know you what
'tis you speak?

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p:
My king! my Jove! I speak to thee, my
heart!

sp.speaker: King.
sp.p:
I know thee not, old man: fall to thy
prayers; How ill white hairs become a fool and jester! I have long drearm'd of such a kind of man, So surfeit-swell'd, so old and so profane; But, being awaked, I do despise my dream. Make less thy body hence, and more thy grace; Leave gormandizing; know the grave doth gape For thee thrice wider than for other men. Reply not to me with a fool-born jest: Presume not that I am the thing I was; For God doth know, so shall the world perceive, That I have turn'd away my former self; So will I those that kept me company. When thou dost hear I am as I have been, Approach me, and thou shalt be as thou wast, The tutor and the feeder of my riots: Till then, I banish thee, on pain of death, As I have done the rest of my misleaders, Not to come near our person by ten mile. For competence of life I will allow you, That lack of means enforce you not to evil: And, as we hear you do reform yourselves, We will, according to your strengths and qualities, Give you advancement. Be it your charge, my
lord, To see perform'd the tenor of our word. Set on.[Exeunt King, etc,

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: Master Shallow, I owe you a thousand pound.

sp.speaker: Shal.
sp.p: Yea, marry, Sir John; which I beseech you to let me have home with me.

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: That can hardly be, Master Shallow. Do not you grieve at this; I shall be sent for in private to him: look you, he must seem thus to the world: fear not your advancements; I will be the man yet that shall make you great.

sp.speaker: Shal.
sp.p: I cannot well perceive how, unless you should give me your doublet and stuff me out with straw. I beseech you, good Sir John, let me have five hundred of my thousand.

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: Sir, I will be as good as my word: this that you heard was but a color.

sp.speaker: Shal.
sp.p: A color that I fear you will die in, Sir John.

sp.speaker: Fal.
Ch. Just.
sp.p:
Go, carry Sir John Falstaff to the
Fleet: Take all his company along with him.

sp.speaker: Fal.
sp.p: My lord, my lord,--

sp.speaker: Ch. Just.
sp.p:
I cannot now speak: I will hear
you soon. Take them away.

sp.speaker: Pist.
sp.p:
Si fortuna me tormenta, spero contenta.
[Exeunt all but Prince John and the
Chief-Justice.

sp.speaker: Lan.
sp.p: I like this fair proceeding of the king's: He hath intent his wonted followers Shall all be very well provided for; But all are banish'd till their conversations Appear more wise and modest to the world.

sp.speaker: Ch. Just.
sp.p: And so they are.

sp.speaker: Lan.
sp.p:
The king hath call'd his parliament, my
lord.

sp.speaker: Ch. Just.
sp.p: He hath.

sp.speaker: Lan.
sp.p: I will lay odds that, ere this yeai expire, We bear our civil swords and native fire As far as France: I heard a bird so sing, Whose music, to my thinking, pleased the king. Come, will you hence? [Exeunt.

div.head: EPILOGUE
div.p: First my fear; then my courtesy; last my speech. My fear is, your displeasure; my courtesy, my duty; and my speech, to beg your pardons. If you look for a good speech now, you undo me: for what I have to say is of mine own making; and what indeed I should say will, I doubt, prove mine own marring. But to the purpose, and so to the venture. Be it known to you, as it is very well, I was lately here in the end of a displeasing play, to pray your patience for it and to promise you a better. I meant indeed to pay you with this; which, if like an ill venture it come unluckily home, I break, and you, my gentle creditors, lose. Here I promised you I would be and here I commit my body to your mercies : bate me some and I will pay you some and, as most debtors do, promise you infinitely. If my tongue cannot entreat you to acquit me, will you command me to use my legs? and yet that were but light payment, to dance out of your debt. But a good conscience will make any possible satisfaction, and so would I. All the gentlewomen here have forgiven me: if the gentlemen will not, then the gentlemen do not agree with the gentlewomen, which was never seen before in such an assembly. One word more, I beseech you. If you be not too much cloyed with fat meat, our humble author will continue the story, with Sir John in it, and make you merry with fair Katharine of France: where, for any thing I know, Falstaff shall die of a sweat, unlessalready a' be killed with your hard opinions; for Oldcastle died a martyr, and this is not the man. My tongue is weary; when my legs are too, I will bid you good night: and so kneel down before you; but, indeed, to pray for the queen.
